history.period: Present complex from the 1970s; legend from the Kalika Purana
history.summary: Major Hindu pilgrimage site in Lohit district on the lower reaches of the Lohit River, about 48 km from Tezu. Per the Kalika Purana legend, the sage Parashurama (6th avatar of Vishnu) washed away the sins of killing the kshatriyas — and, in the local telling, his matricide — in the waters of Brahma Kund here. The original kund established by Assam pilgrims was destroyed in the 1950 earthquake; boulders then embedded in a circular formation in the riverbed, forming the present kund. The small temple complex houses idols of Vishnu and Parashurama, a Devi Renuka shrine, a dashavatar shrine with all ten avatars, and panels depicting the Renuka legend, set amid a dense rudraksha forest inside the Kamlang Reserve Forest. Over 70,000 devotees and sadhus take the holy dip each Makar Sankranti (January) at the Parshuram Kund Mela, called the 'Mahakumbh of the Northeast'. CSV town 'Parasuram Kund' is the site name, not a town; nearest town is Wakro (16 km).

name: Parshuram Kund
town_description: Wakro is a small town in Lohit district at the foothills of the Mishmi Hills, about 16 km from Parshuram Kund. It is the nearest market town and the last roadhead before the pilgrimage site, lying close to the Kamlang Reserve Forest.

travel.railway: New Tinsukia Junction, Assam, about 151 km
travel.road: About 48 km from Tezu and 16 km from Wakro; state-run and private buses and taxis run from Tinsukia, Dibrugarh and Tezu. Descending to the riverbank involves several hundred steps from the temple complex

visitor_information.best_time: January for the Makar Sankranti mela; more generally October to March (winter). The monsoon (June-September) is best avoided
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours; an entry permit is required to reach the site — permits are issued at Dirak and Sunpura check posts, and by the Lohit Deputy Commissioner's office during the mela
